title: The Night Bitcoin Split in Two ⚡ #Shorts
description:
March 11, 2013: Bitcoin split into two chains.
The new version 0.8 accepted a huge block (block 225,430, over 5,000 transactions). Older versions couldn't read it - their database ran out of locks. Mt. Gox and BitPay paused deposits and the price dropped 24%.
Developers chose the old chain, big mining pools downgraded, and about six hours later the chains joined again. 24 blocks were wiped out, and a $10,000 double spend hit OKPay.

Bug or warning? 👇

Not financial advice. Entertainment and education only.
pinned: Would you have picked the old chain or the new one? 👇

scenes.line: March 2013. Bitcoin split into two chains.
And the developers chose to kill the newer one.
It started with an update. Version zero point eight was brand new, but many computers still ran zero point seven.
Then one huge block arrived. It touched over five thousand transactions.
The new computers accepted it. The old ones choked.
It needed over ten thousand database locks. The old version ran out.
Now there were two Bitcoins at the same time.
Mt. Gox and BitPay shut down deposits.
And the price dropped twenty-four percent.
So developers asked the big miners to go back to the old version.
About six hours later, the old chain took the lead, and won.
And someone spent the same ten thousand dollars twice, against OKPay.
One block. Two Bitcoins. Bug, or warning?

headline: ONE BLOCK SPLIT / BITCOIN IN TWO
